bullets.title: ORCL: Strong OCI beat expected tonight; buy into earnings on cloud upside
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag ORCL F1Q27 as a key AI trade signal. MS models OCI revenue +120% y/y vs consensus +115%; a separate regression forecasts $7.2B OCI revenue (~300bps above consensus). Bull/base cases imply 20-30% three-year EPS CAGRs. RPO build, stable OpenAI funding confirmation, and New Mexico Stargate pipeline will be scrutinized. Mizuho hosting post-earnings debrief call tonight at 9pm ET.

bullets.title: ADBE: Sell any beat enthusiasm; AI monetization not accelerating this quarter
bullets.body: Desk view is to fade ADBE on any post-earnings enthusiasm — management already reset 2H bookings lower last quarter, so a beat is likely but unlikely to shift skepticism. Core debate is whether AI drives incremental ARR or just defends the existing franchise; consensus view is AI adoption outpaces monetization with no inflection this quarter. Stock seen as 'cheap for a reason.'

bullets.title: META: JPM upgrades to Overweight, $820 PT on AI Models & Agents
bullets.body: JPMorgan (Doug Anmuth) upgrades META to Overweight from neutral with an $820 price target, citing commercial availability of AI Models and Agents. Hedgeye separately flipped META from short to long. META Muse jumped to #3 personal assistant and was up ~6% on 9/9, driving rotation within Mag7 away from GOOGL/AMZN.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 event mixed — foldable Duo niche at $1,999; Pro pricing +$100 only
bullets.body: iPhone Duo foldable launches at $1,999–$3,200 with fluid form factor (barely noticeable crease per MS hands-on) but weak camera/battery vs Pro; base models delayed to spring 2027. Pro/Pro Max pricing up only $100 vs $150–200 feared. A20 Pro chip (2nm, 50% more memory bandwidth); C2 modem added but QCOM retains higher modem share than expected. Analyst views split: Jefferies underperform on volume risk, Goldman buy on ASP/revenue expansion. 57% of installed base on hardware older than iPhone 15 Pro.

bullets.title: NVDA: August rack ramp +27% m/m; $500B capital partnership framed as 'Balance Sheet-as-a-Service'
bullets.body: MS estimates GB200/300 August rack output ~8,400 units (+27% m/m) with CY26 forecast of 80–85K racks at 100%+ y/y growth. The $500B+ capital partnership is viewed positively for chip financing and AI issuance; revenue-sharing arrangements and neocloud dynamics are the key debate. DoJ separately opened a probe into NVDA's Groq licensing deal for potential antitrust concerns.

bullets.title: MSFT: Consumption-based pricing (UBB) flagged as major near-term growth driver; E7 'incredibly strong start'
bullets.body: Citi TMT takeaway: MSFT's usage-based billing launched June 1 and Spataro calls it a 'big deal' with potential to drive sequential q/q growth. E7 (new premium tier introduced F4Q) off to an 'incredibly strong start' though not broken out separately. Three near-term goals: drive USL penetration from 30M+, grow UBB consumption q/q, and develop IQ data layer to solve the AI data bottleneck. Jefferies separately reiterates buyer with AMZN and GOOGL as preferred hyperscalers on relative value.

bullets.title: CHTR: Cox synergies >$1B (~50% achievable quickly); ARPU inflection expected Q3; leverage target cut to 3.5x
bullets.body: CHTR CFO at Citi TMT: broadband competition unchanged from Q1 but gross-add weakness (not churn) is the headwind — video+broadband bundles cut churn ~40%, streaming activation cuts it 55%. Broadband ARPU expected to improve sequentially in Q3 after mid-July price actions. Mobile at only ~20% internet penetration represents a significant growth opportunity. Leverage target lowered to 3.5x with buybacks preserved.

bullets.title: DELL: AI demand still accelerating with multi-year S-curve; storage becoming second major growth leg
bullets.body: DELL at Citi TMT framed AI infrastructure demand as still accelerating (not peaking) with 6,500 AI Factory customers in early adoption. Supply remains the binding constraint — gap expected to tighten next year. Storage now guided double-digit full-year growth as a durable second leg. AI server margins staying mid-single digits while operating leverage (~8% OpEx/revenue) becomes the structural earnings driver. Commercial PC demand weak for next 2–3 quarters.

bullets.title: T: AT&T CFO guides wireless above full-year, fiber potentially below; double-digit EPS growth on track
bullets.body: AT&T at Citi TMT: wireless service revenue likely to exceed full-year guidance; fiber may come in slightly below. Company on track for double-digit EPS growth in 2026 and returning ~100% of FCF. Convergence strategy (bundled wireless+fiber) targeting lower churn and higher LTV. AI-driven demand centered on higher-capacity connectivity and security; >85% of footprint off copper by year-end.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM reiterates OW $185 PT as leading agentic commerce platform
bullets.body: JPM (Bryan Smilek) reiterates Overweight on SHOP with $185 PT, positioning it as the leading agentic platform with low AI disruption risk. ETSY separately announced partnership with Remitly for international seller payouts but faces risk that autonomous agents could make Etsy Ads less important, pressuring margins.

bullets.title: CRM: Fin acquisition closed at ~$3.6B; only ~5% of customers on premium AE1 edition
bullets.body: Salesforce completed its $3.6B acquisition of Fin (AI customer service agent resolving queries across chat, email, WhatsApp, phone, and Slack) with no change to FY27 guidance or capital return program. GS Communacopia note separately highlighted only ~5% of CRM customers are on the AE1 premium edition (60–80% price uplift), representing substantial monetization runway.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY August GGR fell 9.7% y/y; market share slipped to 33.4% from 35.0%
bullets.body: New York online sports betting GGR declined 5.5% y/y to $168.5M in August with total handle +15.3% y/y (hold% compressed). DraftKings GGR fell 9.7% y/y to $56.3M with market share dropping to 33.4% from 35.0%; handle grew 5.9% but hold compressed to 9.2% from 10.7%. FanDuel was stable at 38% share while Fanatics gained to 11.2%.

bullets.title: MU/SNDK: Deepseek V4.1 Flash compresses KV cache 437x — mixed read for memory
bullets.body: Deepseek V4.1 Flash uses a new Causal Encoder-Decoder architecture reducing KV cache HBM requirements by 75% and SSD storage by 87.5% vs prior generation (~437x bytes/token improvement). Analyst view: token growth no longer translates proportionally into memory-bit demand; creates a stock-picker environment within memory rather than a sector-wide thesis.

bullets.title: INTC/AMD/MU/NVDA: Notebook ODM shipments -26% y/y in August; 2026 forecast cut to -10-15%
bullets.body: KeyBank cuts 2026 notebook shipment forecast to -10–15% y/y from -8–12% after August miss (11.7M units vs 14.1M estimate). All major ODMs missed. Memory price increases driving elevated channel inventory and slowing sell-through. PC-exposed names AMD, INTC, MU flagged as negatively impacted.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: DoJ expands probe into Fox-Roku acquisition
bullets.body: The US DoJ expanded its antitrust probe into Fox's proposed acquisition of Roku, adding regulatory overhang to the deal. Separately, DoJ opened a probe into Nvidia's Groq licensing deal. Wolfe Research hosting a video advertising dinner Sept 23 with Fox/Roku merger as a key discussion topic alongside WBD ad leadership.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Peacock hits 48M subs and quarterly profitability; next growth from ARPU and engagement
bullets.body: Comcast at BofA conference: Peacock reached quarterly profitability and 48M subscribers in Q2, with next phase of growth relying on wholesale distribution, YouTube bundling, and sports (NBA tracking ahead of expectations in year one). Advertising mix shifted from ~30% to ~60% in live sports and streaming. NBCUniversal independence framing aimed at increasing partnership optionality.

bullets.title: BKNG/ABNB/EXPE: OTA stocks down 8-18% from highs on AI agent travel booking threat
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags Meta's AI Agent Muse and Instinct's AI Agent as catalysts driving BKNG, ABNB, and EXPE down 8–18% from recent highs. Instinct generates direct payment links for travel bookings — described as a game-changer though still small scale. Separately, Airbnb faces stricter EU short-term rental rules per StreetAccount ESG digest.

bullets.title: CRDO/STX: Semis down 3-4% pre-market; CRDO -40% from YTD highs despite optics transition visibility
bullets.body: Pre-market weakness across semis: CRDO -3.3%, STX -3.2%, WDC -3.6%, MU -2.9%, ALAB -3.7%. GS Communacopia note separately highlighted CRDO is down ~40% from YTD highs despite improved optics transition visibility, and STX is well-positioned on GM/ASP expansion relative to DRAM/NAND peers.

bullets.title: TSLA: Key XLY weight (17.7%) with earnings Oct 22 — desk recommends put spread hedge
bullets.body: 22V and Hedgeye both flag TSLA's outsized 17.7% XLY weight as a tactical risk ahead of Oct 22 earnings; XLY fell 4.6% on TSLA's last report (7/23). TSLA rallied ~24% from July lows despite broader consumer weakness. Recommended hedge: Buy XLY Oct 23 110/100 put spread for ~$1.70–$1.90 offering ~5:1 max payoff.

bullets.title: NFLX: Florida AG sues over minor data misrepresentation and binge-watching harms
bullets.body: Netflix was sued by the Florida Attorney General over alleged misrepresentation of minor data collection practices and facilitating binge-watching harms to children. This adds to regulatory headline risk for the stock.
